646: SNFG symbols: green mannose, blue N-acetylglucosamine, yellow galactose, purple sialic acid, red fucose. The high-mannose glycan received in the ER is trimmed then rebuilt into a complex glycan from one cisterna to the next.
648: Sorting station: tyrosine sulfation, cleavage of pro-proteins by furin, mannose-6-phosphate receptors towards endosomes (clathrin/AP-1), vesicles towards the plasma membrane.
649: pH ≈ 6.0. Galactosyltransferases and sialyltransferases finish the antennae of complex glycans.
651: GlcNAc-transferase I, mannosidase II then GlcNAc-transferase II: from high-mannose to complex glycan; core fucosylation.
652: pH ≈ 6.7. Arrival of COPII vesicles. Mannosidases I remove mannoses (Man₉ → Man₅); GlcNAc-phosphotransferase tags lysosomal enzymes with mannose-6-phosphate; ER resident proteins (KDEL motif) go back in COPI vesicles.
655: Lollipops: glycosyltransferases anchored in the membrane; beads: glycoproteins and their glycans.
657: Entry through the protein import pathway: TOM complex (outer membrane) then TIM23 (inner membrane). Narrative licence: only unfolded chains get through.
659: Entry through the Sec61 translocon, like a nascent chain (narrative licence).
661: Entry like the contents of a vesicle fusing with the cisterna (narrative licence).
666: You are RNA polymerase II, in front of the ${G.sy} gene. The general transcription factors install you on the promoter. ${pm[0]} The TFIIH helicase opens the double helix: the template strand enters your active site.
667: Assembly of the pre-initiation complex: ${pm[1]} The XPB translocase of TFIIH (ATP) melts 11 to 15 bp: open complex. Your CTD (52 heptads Y₁S₂P₃T₄S₅P₆S₇) is unphosphorylated (grey).
668: Which TFIIH subunit opens the promoter?
672: First phosphodiester bonds: the RNA starts with the ${sqR(0,1)} of the +1 site. The TFIIH kinase phosphorylates your CTD tail (it turns orange): you let go of the promoter.
673: After a few abortive cycles (< 10 nt), the RNA–DNA hybrid reaches 8–9 bp and you leave the promoter. CDK7 (TFIIH) phosphorylates Ser5 and Ser7 of the CTD: the link with Mediator breaks, the capping enzyme and SET1/COMPASS are recruited (H3K4me3 on the 5′ nucleosomes). TFIID stays in place for re-initiation.
674: Which CTD mark is the signature of initiation?
678: At 25 nucleotides the 5′ end of the RNA emerges: a 7-methylguanosine cap is added at once, linked “head to head”. It protects the RNA and will serve for export then translation. The CBC complex (white) binds it.
679: The capping enzyme RNGTT, docked on the Ser5-P CTD, removes the γ phosphate (triphosphatase) then transfers a GMP: a 5′–5′ triphosphate linkage. RNMT/RAM methylates N7 (cap 0, m⁷GpppN); CMTR1 methylates the 2′-OH of the first nucleotide (cap 1), a mark of “self” for innate immunity. CBC (CBP80/CBP20) binds the cap.
680: Which linkage joins the cap to the first nucleotide?
685: Compulsory stop around +40: two factors, DSIF and NELF, hold you back. This is a major checkpoint of gene expression. The kinase P-TEFb frees you by phosphorylating NELF and your CTD (which will turn cyan).${pm[2]}
686: Pause between +20 and +60: DSIF (SPT4/SPT5) and NELF immobilise you. P-TEFb (CDK9/cyclin T1, released from the 7SK snRNP, recruited by BRD4 or the super elongation complex) phosphorylates NELF (ejected), SPT5 (which becomes a positive factor) and Ser2 of the CTD. PAF1C and SPT6 join you.${pm[2]}
691: You race along at ≈ 30 nucleotides per second. At each step a nucleotide complementary to the template strand is added to the 3′ end of the RNA. The AUG start codon (${G.cs==CM?`+${G.cs+1}`:`nt ${CM+1} of the mRNA, in exon ${XN[G.cs]+1}`}) ${G.cs<x4?`has just gone by`:`has not come out yet`}, but nothing will be translated before the cytoplasm.
692: Addition cycle: NTP entry, closure of the trigger loop, two-Mg²⁺ catalysis (attack of the 3′-OH on the α phosphate, release of pyrophosphate), translocation. A bubble of 12 to 14 nt. FACT and SPT6 take nucleosomes apart then rebuild them; RNF20/40 ubiquitinates H2B. TFIIS restarts the polymerase after backtracking by cleaving the RNA.
693: Which group of the RNA attacks the incoming NTP?
696: The end of exon 1 has emerged. The small ribonucleoprotein U1 (light blue) recognises the start of the intron, which almost always begins with GU: this is the splice donor site.
697: The 5′ end of U1 snRNA pairs with the donor site (here ${sqR(e1-3,3)}|${sqR(e1,6)}; consensus MAG|GURAGU): E complex. U1-70K interacts with SR proteins bound to the exon and with the CTD. U1 also protects the transcript from premature polyadenylation.${pm[3]}
698: How does U1 recognise the donor site?
699: By base pairing with its snRNA
702: Slow motion — A complex: U2 at the branch point
703: Intron 1 (${nf(NI?G.I[0].n:0)} nt${NI&&G.I[0].n>i1-e1?`, of which ${i1-e1} modelled`:``}) has fully emerged. The U2 snRNP (green) binds the branch point, a key adenosine, while U2AF (orange) marks the end of the intron, which ends with AG.
704: SF1 then U2: U2 snRNA pairs around the branch point (consensus yUnAy${b1.d?`; best-ranked candidate in this sequence: ${rU(b1.s)}, A at ${b1.d} nt from the acceptor, ${b1.v<4?`only a partial match to the consensus, `:``}predicted and not experimentally validated`:``}) leaving the adenosine bulged out, 2′-OH exposed; SF3B1 holds it (gene mutated in myelodysplastic syndromes). U2AF2 binds the polypyrimidine tract, U2AF1 the AG (here ${sqR(i1-12,12)}|${sqR(i1,3)}). A complex, ATP-dependent (Prp5, UAP56).${pm[4]}
705: Which nucleotide serves as the branch point?
709: Slow motion — B complex: the U4/U6·U5 tri-snRNP
710: Three more snRNPs arrive joined in one block: U4, U6 and U5. The spliceosome is complete but still inactive: U6, the future catalytic core, is kept on a leash by U4.
711: The U4/U6·U5 tri-snRNP (≈ 1.5 MDa) joins the A complex: pre-B then B complex. U6 is paired with U4 there, hence inactive; loop I of U5 settles against exon 1; Prp8 forms the scaffold of the future active site.
714: Two helicases remodel everything: U1 and U4 leave. U6 takes the place of U1 on the donor site and pairs with U2. The branch point then attacks the start of the intron: exon 1 is detached and the intron forms a lariat.
715: Prp28 releases U1; Brr2 unwinds U4/U6; the NTC complex (Prp19) stabilises the assembly: activated B complex, then B* after Prp2. U6 (ACAGAGA on the donor site, internal loop coordinating 2 Mg²⁺) and U2 form an active site made of RNA: the spliceosome is a ribozyme. Step 1: the 2′-OH of the adenosine attacks the phosphate of the donor site → free exon 1 (3′-OH) and a lariat with a 2′–5′ bond.
719: Second move: the free end of exon 1 attacks the end of the intron. Exons 1 and 2 are joined; the lariat is released then destroyed. An EJC complex (pink) is deposited just before the junction: it keeps the memory of splicing.
